items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The names are clear, the stream format is documented in the package doc and the closer ordering has comments. The cap still applies: business logic uses single-letter names such as `k := make([]byte, KeySize)` and `w = ew`, alongside short names like `ew` and `dr`.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Config/LoadKey and the stream code are split into separate files, and functions are short and single-purpose (init/flush/finish/next, getEncryptor). There is no dead code. Two small nits: the key-length check is duplicated in NewEncryptor and DecryptReader, and argon2 was used instead of the vendored pbkdf2.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Errors are wrapped with sentinels (ErrInvalidKey, ErrIntegrity, ErrTruncated) and the HMAC is compared in constant time with hmac.Equal. Chunk lengths are checked against min/max bounds, and sizes are named constants. Close is idempotent, writes are refused after close (ErrClosed), and the key is loaded before any storage is touched.

items.name: Interface changes limited to the specified ones
items.name_zh: 接口变更仅限题目要求
items.evidence: The mandated changes are done and unencrypted output is unchanged. However, `storage.PathGenerator(gzip, unique)` keeps its old signature and hardcodes `EnsureFileName(filename, gzip, false, unique)`, which wraps the change instead of updating callers. It also adds extra exports (ErrInvalidConfig, KeySource* constants, Magic, etc.).
